hits.query: pit entry closed during the race, can a car enter the pit lane
hits.text:
34.15 In exceptional circumstances the Race Director may ask for the pit entry to be closed during the
sprint session or the race for safety reasons.
a) At such times drivers may only enter the pit lane in order for essential and entirely evident
repairs to be carried out to the car.
b) A penalty in accordance with Article 54.3d) will be imposed on any driver who, in the
opinion of the stewards, entered the pit lane for any other reason whilst it was closed.

hits.citation: Pit entry closed: no tyre stop permitted
hits.query: pit entry closed during the race, can a car enter the pit lane
hits.text: When the Race Director closes the pit entry for safety reasons (Article 34.15), drivers may only enter the pit lane for essential and entirely evident repairs. A driver who enters for any other reason, such as a tyre change, receives a penalty under Article 54.3(d), a ten second stop-and-go. A planned stop on a lap while the pit entry is closed must move to the first lap after it reopens.

hits.citation: 2023 Singapore GP: Mercedes double-stack under the VSC
hits.query: entering the pits to change tyres while the safety car is deployed
hits.text: 2023 Singapore Grand Prix. Car 31 (OCO) completed its last lap on lap 43 and the Virtual Safety Car was deployed on lap 44. Mercedes pitted cars 44 (HAM) and 63 (RUS) at the end of lap 44 from hard to new medium tyres; cars may enter the pits under the VSC to change tyres. Measured against the non-stopping leader, Hamilton lost 19.4 s and Russell 16.7 s across their in- and out-laps, against about 30.5 s for a green-flag stop at this circuit. Car 55 (SAI) stayed out on hards and won from car 4 (NOR); Hamilton finished third.

hits.citation: Wet races: the two dry-compound rule no longer applies
hits.query: Article 30.5(m) at least two different specifications of dry-weather tyres unless intermediate or wet used
hits.text: Article 30.5(m) requires each driver to use at least two different dry-weather tyre specifications in the race, unless the driver used intermediate or wet-weather tyres during the race. After an intermediate or wet stint a car may finish on a single dry compound. In a dry race, failing to use a second dry specification leads to disqualification, unless the race is suspended and cannot be restarted, in which case 30 seconds are added to the driver's elapsed time. The paragraph letter differs by year: 30.5(n) in the 2023 regulations, 30.5(m) in 2024 and 2025.
